trajectory_summary: The agent located the provided MATPOWER snapshot (Turn 1), discovered required numerical/optimization libraries were missing (Turn 2), and worked around the externally-managed Python environment by creating a virtualenv and installing numpy/cvxpy/solvers (Turns 3–4). It parsed network.json into MATPOWER matrices (Turns 5–6), formulated and solved a DC-OPF with reserve co-optimization for a base case and a counterfactual case where the 64–1501 line RATE_A was increased by 20% (Turn 7). After initially producing clearly mis-scaled LMPs (Turn 8), it corrected LMP scaling/sign, re-solved both cases, and rewrote report.json (Turn 9), then re-validated key outputs (Turn 10) and confirmed the target line was binding in the base case but not binding in the counterfactual (Turn 11). The run ended with report.json created and populated with costs, per-bus LMPs, reserve MCP, binding lines, and an impact analysis (Turn 12).
what_worked: Turn 1: Correctly found the required input file (“./network.json”).
Turn 4: Successfully created a virtualenv and installed required packages; evidence: “Successfully installed … numpy … cvxpy … clarabel …”.
Turn 5: Correctly loaded MATPOWER arrays and confirmed dimensions (bus (2869,13), gen (510,10), branch (4582,13), gencost (510,7)) and reserve inputs (reserve_requirement 5923.5).
Turn 7: Executed two solves and wrote report.json; evidence: “Solved base cost: 3073359.46”, “Solved cf cost: 3069798.51”, “Target branches: [1446]”, “Wrote report.json”.
Turn 9: Corrected LMP computation and regenerated report.json; evidence: “largest lmp drops [(64, 143.85, 39.47), …]” with realistic magnitudes and “wrote report.json”.
Turn 11: Verified the specific study question (whether relaxing 64–1501 relieves congestion on that element); evidence: “target in base binding? True” and “target in cf binding? False”.

issues.evidence: Turn 2 shows “numpy import failed” and “cvxpy import failed”; Turn 3 pip install failed with “externally-managed-environment”.
issues.cause: Execution environment disallowed system-wide pip installs and lacked needed optimization libraries; required a virtual environment workaround.

issues.evidence: After Turn 7, Turn 8 validation shows extreme/implausible LMPs, e.g. “base_lmp: 3267656.65” and negative hundreds of thousands, indicating a scaling/sign error in LMP extraction from duals.
issues.cause: Incorrect conversion from power-balance dual variables to $/MWh (used multiplication by baseMVA instead of appropriate sign/scaling), leading to nonsensical prices until corrected.

issues.evidence: Even after relieving the target constraint, binding line count increased from 24 (base) to 25 (counterfactual) per Turn 10, meaning congestion likely shifted to other constraints.
issues.cause: Relaxing one transmission limit can re-route flows and cause other lines to become (near-)binding; the report’s congestion_relieved flag only checks the modified line, not system-wide congestion reduction.

outcome_rationale: The agent produced report.json with the requested structure and solved both base and counterfactual cases, and it verified the target line was binding in the base case and not binding after the 20% limit increase (Turns 9–11), indicating the required “what-if relax it” analysis was completed despite an earlier LMP scaling mistake that was later fixed.
